events.title: Community Sing
events.description: Join us on the first Tuesday of every month for community singing. Simply show up (registration is not required) and join the circle of voices. Music will be taught the night of; all voices are welcome to gather and be led in song. There are no auditions or music to read, no performances, and little to no accompanying instrumentation. Community Sing is an entirely oral tradition for people of all ages! Unlike a choir, Community Sing is not divided by traditional voice parts or vocal range. Some songs are sung all together, as call-and-response, in a round, or in taught parts. Community Sing is also non-denominational. This recurring monthly event has no cover charge, though donations are always appreciated. Thank you Chickadee-Dee-Dee for leading us in song!

events.description: The Arrowhead Library System is pleased to present Soldiers of the American Revolution with Arn Kind of Historical Experiences. These free history events will travel to participating ALS libraries October 14-November 20, 2026. On this 250th Anniversary of the Declaration of Independence join Arn Kind for an event all about the American Revolution. events.title: Jill D. Swenson: Exploring Land, Loss, and Legacy
events.description: Author Talk | Jill D. Swenson | Exploring Land, Loss, and Legacy Wednesday, November 4, 5:30 - 6:30 p.m. Grand Marais Public Library Free, open to all Set in the Lake of the Woods region of northern Minnesota, Jill D. Swenson’s memoir, The Land of Everlasting Sky: A Memoir of Loss and Legacy on Lake of the Woods, brings together family history, personal grief, and questions of land, identity, and belonging. After returning to her mother’s hometown following her death, Swenson begins investigating the region’s history and the experiences of the descendants of Kakaygeesick, an Ojibway spiritual leader. Her research leads to a friendship with Kakaygeesick’s great-grandson and a deeper examination of land allotment, tribal membership, and federal Indian policy. As she explores these histories, Swenson also confronts the losses and family estrangements that have shaped her own life. Both personal and historical in scope, The Land of Everlasting Sky considers how the past continues to influence our understanding of ourselves, our communities, and our relationships to the land. Books will be available for purchase at the event through Drury Lane Books. Jill D.

events.title: Ian Alexy
events.description: Troubadour 21st Century is the new record by singer-songwriter Ian Alexy. Best known for his work with Americana duo Hobo Nephews Of Uncle Frank, Ian expands the possibilities on Troubadour 21st Century with rock grooves and spine-tingling electric guitar flourishes. This is Ian Alexy’s fifth album as a solo artist, in addition to five albums with Hobo Nephews Of Uncle Frank. Hobo Nephews first earned their live reputation by opening a sold-out national tour for Trampled By Turtles before touring all over the United States as a headliner. Their 2015 song Old Number 4 was featured on CBS Sports.com and soon after went viral. Ian has received critical acclaim for his work as a solo artist as well. events.title: Ely Area Writer’s Group
events.description: The mission of the Ely Area Writers Group (formerly Writers Read) is to encourage writers to write. Writers tend to hide their work. For most, the only thing worse than rejection is having something printed that isn’t perfect, so we give gentle suggestions for edits and cheer all the good bits. When someone joins our group, we add their email to our list. Before our monthly meetings, anyone can submit something they’ve written to the group via email. Any genre is welcome. The author may be specific about what response they want (does this essay flow, or is this character believable, or which images stick with you?) or they can let the others respond on any aspect that strikes them. Some members submit work every month, others may share something only a few times a year. Registration is not required; simply show up!

events.title: Theatre North Presents: The Dining Room
events.description: The opening production for the 2026 – 2027 Theatre North Season is The Dining Room. Synopsis: Set in the dining room of a typical well-to-do household, The Dining Room is a mosaic of interrelated scenes – some funny, some touching, some rueful – which, taken together, create an in-depth portrait of vanishing traditions of the American upper middle class. The actors change roles, as they portray a wide variety of characters, from little boys to stern grandfathers, and from giggling teenage girls to Irish housemaids. Each vignette introduces a new set of people and events (spanning decades): a father lectures his son on grammar and politics; a boy returns from boarding school to discover his mother’s infidelity; a senile grandmother doesn’t recognize her own sons at Christmas dinner; a daughter, her marriage a shambles, pleads futilely to return home. Dovetailing swiftly and smoothly, the varied scenes coalesce, ultimately, into a theatrical experience of exceptional range, compassionate humor and abundant humanity. Show Times are: November 5, 6, 7, 13 and 14 at 7:00pm Matinees November 8 and 15 at 2:00pm TICKET INFORMATION IS FOUND HERE.

Andreas Klein’s career as orchestra soloist and recitalist has taken him to the world’s most prestigious venues from London’s Wigmore Hall, Berlin’s Philharmonic Hall, New York’s Carnegie Hall and Alice Tully Hall, to Washington, DC’s Kennedy Center and National Gallery. In Europe as well as in the USA, Mexico, and the Middle East, he has gained critical acclaim for his performances in major cities such as Berlin, Rome, Milan, Bern, Leipzig, Dresden, New York, Los Angeles, Chicago, Washington, DC, Cleveland, Damascus, Mexico City, Calgary, and the Ravinia Festival in Chicago.

events.title: Spirit of the Wilderness Community Art Show, "The Art of Sabbath," Opening Reception
events.description: The Johnson Heritage Post Art Gallery is pleased to host the 15th annual Spirit of the Wilderness Community Art Show, themed "The Art of Sabbath." The exhibit opens with a public reception on Friday, November 6, 2026, from 5 p.m. to 7 p.m., and runs through November 29, 2026. This gallery exhibition centers around winter in the north, which is a time of survival: physically, mentally, and spiritually. This exhibit explores how artists navigate the season, whether hibernating, ice fishing, or moving south, and looks at how we not only survive, but thrive, during the northern winter. Drawing on the ancient practice of Sabbath, participating artists showcase how they rest, recover, and restore through physical stillness and spiritual reconnection. The resulting works highlight these personal reflections across all mediums.

events.title: Theatre North Presents: The Dining Room
events.description: The opening production for the 2026 – 2027 Theatre North Season is The Dining Room. Synopsis: Set in the dining room of a typical well-to-do household, The Dining Room is a mosaic of interrelated scenes – some funny, some touching, some rueful – which, taken together, create an in-depth portrait of vanishing traditions of the American upper middle class. The actors change roles, as they portray a wide variety of characters, from little boys to stern grandfathers, and from giggling teenage girls to Irish housemaids. Each vignette introduces a new set of people and events (spanning decades): a father lectures his son on grammar and politics; a boy returns from boarding school to discover his mother’s infidelity; a senile grandmother doesn’t recognize her own sons at Christmas dinner; a daughter, her marriage a shambles, pleads futilely to return home. Dovetailing swiftly and smoothly, the varied scenes coalesce, ultimately, into a theatrical experience of exceptional range, compassionate humor and abundant humanity. Show Times are: November 5, 6, 7, 13 and 14 at 7:00pm Matinees November 8 and 15 at 2:00pm TICKET INFORMATION IS FOUND HERE.

Teague Alexy
events.description: Award-winning Duluth-based musician, author and storyteller Teague Alexy is probably best known for his Americana songwriting in the national touring brothers duo Hobo Nephews of Uncle Frank. Teague’s songwriting is clearly influenced by his home in Minnesota, as well as his childhood in New Jersey, and life as a travelling musical hobo. Teague's storytelling has deeper roots to his Irish ancestry. The name ‘Teague’ was once used to describe the storytelling poets who travelled ancient Ireland. New album "Effervescent" available 2/14/16. Teague's second album of 2017 is a collaboration with Trampled By Turtles mandolin player Erik Berry. 'Irish American' features nine traditional Irish favorites, including "Whiskey in the Jar," "The Wild Colonial Boy" and "Mountain Dew," as well as two original songs. Teague’s first album of 2017, Circuit Sessions, combines multiple musical genres into a powerful new collection of Teague’s poetic songs with the lionstrong production and rhythm section of Eric Pollard (Actual Wolf) and Steve Garrington (Low) joined by Minneapolis guitarist Jake Hanson. Teague also has a new musical and storytelling podcast “Wisecracks & Roadside Flats.”

events.title: Sew a Sámi-Style Leather Bag or Pouch (2 session class)
events.address: 209 E Sheridan St, Ely, MN 55731-1451, United States, Ely
events.description: Traditionally used to carry precious commodities like coffee, tobacco and sugar – the Sámi-style leather pouch has been adapted for use by bush craftsmen the world over due to its durable and practical design! Sew and decorate your own pouch while learning about the history of the Sámi in Northern Europe and North America. Highlights of the class include: ● Walk through every step from start to finish to make your personal pouch or bag. ● Work with Swedish reindeer leather, fish leather, wool, woven pewter, glass beads and bone to customize your pouch or bag. ● Gain hands-on experience with Sámi-style sewing and decorative techniques. ● Learn about the culture, techniques, and spiritual connections that make Sámi duodji (traditional handicrafts) so special!

events.title: Spirit of the Wilderness Community Art Show, "The Art of Sabbath," Gallery Exhibition
events.address: Johnson Heritage Post Art Gallery, 115 W. Wisconsin Street, Grand Marais, MN, 55604, United States
events.description: The Johnson Heritage Post Art Gallery is pleased to host the 15th annual Spirit of the Wilderness Community Art Show, themed "The Art of Sabbath." This gallery exhibition centers around winter in the north, which is a time of survival: physically, mentally, and spiritually. This exhibit explores how artists navigate the season, whether hibernating, ice fishing, or moving south, and looks at how we not only survive, but thrive, during the northern winter. Drawing on the ancient practice of Sabbath, participating artists showcase how they rest, recover, and restore through physical stillness and spiritual reconnection. The resulting works highlight these personal reflections across all mediums. The exhibit opens with a public reception on Friday, November 6, 2026, from 5 p.m. to 7 p.m., and runs through November 29, 2026. JHP is currently operating under a winter schedule and is not open every day.

events.title: Chamber Music Up North – Sangam: Where East Meets West
events.venue: Spirit of the Lake Community Arts
events.description: 2026 edition of the annual Chamber Music Up North series presents SANGAM, a performance featuring works that are heavily influenced by Indian classical music and features compositions by Juhi Bansal, Asha Srinivasan, Reena Esmail, Nina Shekhar and Shruthi Rajasekar. The word SANGAM derived from Sanskrit and translates to “confluence” referring to a combination of Western and Indian classical music idioms. Audience members will learn about the basic elements of Indian classical music, such as raga and tala, and will be able to experience how these ancient forms are used in contemporary classical music. The concert will include non-traditional seating and stage set up for the performers and a short Meet&Greet with musicians following the performance. Performers include TCCC Artistic Director cellist Magdalena Sas and guest artists: flutist Paula Gudmundson (Professor of Music at University of Minnesota Duluth and McKnight Fellow), violist Laila Zakzook ( Isaura String Quartet), and double bassist Rolf Erdahl ( Professor of Bass at Gustavus Adolphus College).

events.title: Live Music: Balterdash
events.description: Balterdash is Sue Orfield (tenor sax & vocals), Dustin DeGolier (guitars & vocals), John Utphall (keys, fiddle & vocals), and Randy Sinz (basses & vocals) We take great pride in performing our original songs, mixed in with unique arrangements of carefully selected cover tunes. Our sound is a rich fusion of Bluegrass, Americana, and Celtic influences, creating a vibrant and engaging musical experience that resonates with a wide range of listeners. Sue Orfield is an award winning tenor saxophonist, composer and educator who tours internationally and has recorded on hundreds of albums. She makes her home in the Chippewa Valley of Wisconsin. Over the years Sue has shared the stage with many musical greats, among them Bo Diddley, Bobby McFerrin, The Indigo Girls, Ann Wilson (Heart), Dizzy Gillespie, Ivan Neville, and Jo Dee Messina. Dustin DeGolier is a freelance musician serving Northwest Wisconsin. A native of Cumberland, WI, Dustin maintains a frequent performance schedule both solo and with a wide array of groups playing jazz, rock, Americana, blues and more.

events.title: Theatre North Presents: The Dining Room
events.description: The opening production for the 2026 – 2027 Theatre North Season is The Dining Room. Synopsis: Set in the dining room of a typical well-to-do household, The Dining Room is a mosaic of interrelated scenes – some funny, some touching, some rueful – which, taken together, create an in-depth portrait of vanishing traditions of the American upper middle class. The actors change roles, as they portray a wide variety of characters, from little boys to stern grandfathers, and from giggling teenage girls to Irish housemaids. Each vignette introduces a new set of people and events (spanning decades): a father lectures his son on grammar and politics; a boy returns from boarding school to discover his mother’s infidelity; a senile grandmother doesn’t recognize her own sons at Christmas dinner; a daughter, her marriage a shambles, pleads futilely to return home. Dovetailing swiftly and smoothly, the varied scenes coalesce, ultimately, into a theatrical experience of exceptional range, compassionate humor and abundant humanity. Show Times are: November 5, 6, 7, 13 and 14 at 7:00pm Matinees November 8 and 15 at 2:00pm TICKET INFORMATION IS FOUND HERE.

events.description: The six men comprising STYX have committed to rocking the Paradise together with audiences far and wide by averaging over 100 shows a year every year since (yes) 1999, and each one of them is committed to making the next show better than the last. Founded in Chicago in 1972, STYX has the unique distinction of being the first band in rock history to have four consecutive certified multimillion-selling albums in a row: 1977’s The Grand Illusion, 1978’s Pieces of Eight, 1979’s Cornerstone, and 1981’s Paradise Theatre. STYX draws from over four decades of barnburning chart hits, joyous singalongs, and harddriving deep cuts. Like a symphony that builds to a satisfying crescendo, a STYX set covers a wide range of stylistic cornerstones.

events.title: Them Coulee Boys
events.description: “A rollicking blend of bluegrass, folk, and rock and roll” - Folk Alley Soren Staff and Beau Janke—co-founders of folk/rock/Americana outfit Them Coulee Boys—met as camp counselors in northern Wisconsin in 2011. Their weekend workshopping of Avett Brothers and classic country tunes led to original songs and adding Soren’s brother Jens on mandolin, Neil Krause on electric bass and Stas Hable on drums. The band’s name is a nod to the glacial melt-carved river valleys they call home, known by early French fur trappers as coulees. Known for wild swings of emotion during sets, it is not unusual to see fans in tears and minutes later dancing with abandon. The honesty and ability to talk and sing about the feelings and emotions that shape them has endeared them to a growing group of fans and friends. Over the course of five albums, the band has garnered international attention and earned press in Americana UK, American Songwriter, Ditty TV, Folk Alley, and The Bluegrass Situation.

events.title: Theatre North Presents: The Dining Room
events.description: The opening production for the 2026 – 2027 Theatre North Season is The Dining Room. Synopsis: Set in the dining room of a typical well-to-do household, The Dining Room is a mosaic of interrelated scenes – some funny, some touching, some rueful – which, taken together, create an in-depth portrait of vanishing traditions of the American upper middle class. The actors change roles, as they portray a wide variety of characters, from little boys to stern grandfathers, and from giggling teenage girls to Irish housemaids. Each vignette introduces a new set of people and events (spanning decades): a father lectures his son on grammar and politics; a boy returns from boarding school to discover his mother’s infidelity; a senile grandmother doesn’t recognize her own sons at Christmas dinner; a daughter, her marriage a shambles, pleads futilely to return home. Dovetailing swiftly and smoothly, the varied scenes coalesce, ultimately, into a theatrical experience of exceptional range, compassionate humor and abundant humanity. Show Times are: November 5, 6, 7, 13 and 14 at 7:00pm Matinees November 8 and 15 at 2:00pm TICKET INFORMATION IS FOUND HERE.

events.description: An Astrophysicist Goes to the Movies – Part I Presented by Roberts Group Tickets on sale now! “An Astrophysicist Goes to the Movies – Part I” From Star Wars to Armageddon to Titanic to The Martian to oddly scientifically literate Beer Commercials. An entertaining and enlightening review of all the science that our favorite movies got wrong, combined with some of the stuff they got right. Incorporates recent films as well as some classics that you may not have known had any science in them at all. ABOUT NEIL DEGRASSE TYSON Neil deGrasse Tyson was born and raised in New York City where he was educated in the public schools clear through his graduation from the Bronx High School of Science. Tyson went on to earn his BA in Physics from Harvard and his PhD in Astrophysics from Columbia. In 2001, Tyson was appointed by President Bush to serve on a twelve-member commission that studied the Future of the U.S. Aerospace Industry. Edmund Fitzgerald: A Great Lakes Memorial
events.address: 3713 Split Rock Lighthouse Rd., Two Harbors, MN
events.description: This annual event commemorates the sinking of the freighter Edmund Fitzgerald and the total loss of the 29 crew members aboard on November 10, 1975. It is also a time to reflect on the memory of all lives lost on the Great Lakes. The lighthouse, fog signal building, and visitor center will be open for visitors. Guides will welcome visitors and provide historic site and shipwreck information. Throughout the day, visitors can watch a film about Edmund Fitzgerald in the visitor center, or join a guided tour exploring the history of Fitzgerald’s final voyage. At 4:15 pm, the lighthouse will temporarily close while the names of the crew are read to the tolling of a ship’s bell, with a rendition of the Naval Hymn. Following the ceremony, the beacon will be lit, and the tower will be open again to tour until close at 6 pm. Be sure to bring a flashlight or headlamp as the grounds and trails are unlit. The weather is unpredictable, please dress accordingly. The event will be streamed on Split Rock’s Facebook Page and the Minnesota Historical Society’s YouTube channel. Tickets are offered online and onsite. Tickets only guarantee you admission to the site and program.

events.title: Pruitt Center Virtual Speaker: Shawn Achor – The Power of Belief
events.description: Join us for the Pruitt Center Fall 2026 Virtual Speaker, Shawn Achor! Conventional wisdom holds that success is determined by talent, intelligence or the circumstances we happen to land in. After more than a decade of research at Harvard and work in 51 countries, Shawn Achor found that the greatest predictor of our future success is something else entirely: the set of beliefs we hold about the world around us. Beliefs are not passive. They shape what we notice, how we interpret setbacks, how much energy and persistence we bring to hard problems and whether we see a challenge as fixed or changeable. And because beliefs spread through teams the same way emotions do, a single person’s belief about what is possible can raise—or quietly cap—the ceiling for an entire organization. In his newest book, The Power of Beliefs, Shawn demonstrates that these beliefs are far more malleable than we assume, and that changing them is one of the fastest levers we have for changing performance.

events.title: Natural Pages: The Death and Life of the Great Lakes by Dan Egan
events.description: A partnership between the Discovery Center and Koller Library, each month we will focus on a different nature-based book each month, with discussions led by either Discovery Center or library staff. Books will be available for checkout at the library in the weeks prior to the meeting. The Great Lakes--Erie, Huron, Michigan, Ontario, and Superior--hold 20 percent of the world's supply of surface fresh water and provide sustenance, work, and recreation for tens of millions of Americans. But they are under threat as never before, and their problems are spreading across the continent. The Death and Life of the Great Lakes is prize-winning reporter Dan Egan's compulsively readable portrait of an ecological catastrophe happening right before our eyes, blending the epic story of the lakes with an examination of the perils they face and the ways we can restore and preserve them for generations to come. This event is free and open to the public. Registration is not required but is appreciated. This month's Natural Pages Reading Group gathering will be held at the Koller Library in Manitowish Waters. events.description: For more than a decade, Amanda Griggs has documented hundreds of moose observations across northern Wisconsin, revealing a story that challenges long-held assumptions about the species. Through photographs, trail camera images, field research, and individual stories like the well-known bull "Pancho," participants will explore the evidence supporting Wisconsin's resident moose population and learn how citizen science has contributed to a greater understanding of these elusive animals. The presentation also highlights ongoing conservation efforts and how the public can become involved in monitoring and protecting Wisconsin's moose. We will serve light appetizers and have a cash bar from 5:00 PM - 6:00 PM, presentation will run from 6:00 PM - 7:00 PM. Registration required by 11/10/26. Program is held at the North Lakeland Discovery Center Main Lodge. $17/Non-Member, $14/Member and $20 at the door for anyone who has not pre-registered. Thursday, November 12th, 5:00 PM - 7:00 PM. events.title: John Louis
events.venue: Sir Benedicts Tavern on the Lake
events.description: Country troubadour John Louis wanders around this world of music, writing and singing heartworn country folk songs. John’s that guy on the bus who sits quietly, looking tired like the rest of us. The difference is he is sitting there composing a song about your life and those painful poignant moments you dust off on the way home between life’s chores. His songs show us our lives and the subtle but important things that become universally important hallmarks of our Midwestern journey. Like church basement rolls at the funeral. Like the small moments on road trips filled with meaning, loss and memory. The tragedies and triumphs that break us and keep us going one more day. John glimpses it all through a poet’s heart. When he stands bravely on a stage with a guitar and begins singing, we get to see it too. And it makes sense for a moment. The songs John writes keep winning awards from prestigious songwriting showcases. Including the Kerrville Folk Festival New Folk competition, Rocky Mountain Folks Festival Songwriter Showcase, and the Great River Folk Fest songwriter contest. (That’s some hot sh-t folks!)

events.title: Tea Talks – Adam Sippola – Presence: Gateway to Healing and Awakening
events.description: Presence: Gateway to Healing and Awakening Presence is the conscious devotion to be with the movements of life. Where inner presence is the cultivation of awareness, living stillness, and flow within the body, in relational presence we commit to a moment-by-moment conscious relationship with the forces of creation alive and moving within us, between us, and among us in the shared group field. We will explore the relationship between presence and the healing of trauma – our unintegrated past, and how inner and relational presence practices can support our embodiment (incarnation), as well as our awakening (transcendence). In this interactive discussion and experience, Adam will lead the group in relational presence practices including meditation, interoception, embodiment, attunement, and relational mindfulness, and he may guide an integration process if anyone present feels called to participate. Welcome to Tea Talks, interesting talks by interesting people about topics they are passionate about, in a cozy and informal space.

events.title: Crafting Traditional Soap
events.description: Friday November 13th 2026, 5:30pm - 7pm Step into the timeless craft of soap making with artisan soap maker Lindsay Larson. In this class, you’ll be guided through the complete process of creating handcrafted soap using reclaimed animal fat; a sustainable, traditional ingredient once used in every homestead kitchen. Together, we’ll explore the alchemy of transforming rendered fat, lye, and botanicals into a cleansing, nourishing bar of soap. You’ll learn about safety practices, temperature control, ingredient selection, and mold preparation, along with tips on sourcing high-quality materials and natural additives. This is a guided learning experience, perfect for anyone curious about the old ways of soap making and eager to bring this lost art back into their own home practice. Consider bringing: A notebook and writing utensil You Receive: Step by step notes on soap making, one bar of the soap made in class.

events.title: Theatre North Presents: The Dining Room
events.description: The opening production for the 2026 – 2027 Theatre North Season is The Dining Room. Synopsis: Set in the dining room of a typical well-to-do household, The Dining Room is a mosaic of interrelated scenes – some funny, some touching, some rueful – which, taken together, create an in-depth portrait of vanishing traditions of the American upper middle class. The actors change roles, as they portray a wide variety of characters, from little boys to stern grandfathers, and from giggling teenage girls to Irish housemaids. Each vignette introduces a new set of people and events (spanning decades): a father lectures his son on grammar and politics; a boy returns from boarding school to discover his mother’s infidelity; a senile grandmother doesn’t recognize her own sons at Christmas dinner; a daughter, her marriage a shambles, pleads futilely to return home. Dovetailing swiftly and smoothly, the varied scenes coalesce, ultimately, into a theatrical experience of exceptional range, compassionate humor and abundant humanity. Show Times are: November 5, 6, 7, 13 and 14 at 7:00pm Matinees November 8 and 15 at 2:00pm TICKET INFORMATION IS FOUND HERE.

events.description: Friday, November 13, 2026 | DECC Symphony Hall | 7:00pm Presented by Pepper Entertainment HERE ABOUT THE OAK RIDGE BOYS For more than 50 years, The Oak Ridge Boys have defined one of the most recognizable sounds in American music, blending four-part harmonies with an energetic stage presence that has earned them Grammy, CMA, ACM, and Dove Awards. With a legacy that stretches from their Gospel roots in the 1940s to their rise as Country‐Pop hitmakers, the group—Duane Allen, Joe Bonsall, William Lee Golden, and Richard Sterban—has delivered classics like Elvira, Bobbie Sue, American Made, and Thank God for Kids. Their music has produced multiple gold and platinum albums, over 30 Top Ten hits, and collaborations with icons ranging from Johnny Cash and Paul Simon to George Jones and Ray Charles. Today’s performing members are Duane Allen, William Lee Golden, Richard Sterban, and Ben James. The Oak Ridge Boys remain one of the most enduring and dynamic touring acts in the world, known for a high‐energy show that celebrates both their rich history and their continued evolution.

events.title: Live Music: Sister Veery w/ Eldri Snow
events.description: Sister Veery is a Duluth-based electric folk rock band whose spacious sound blends electric piano and lilting vocal harmonies with an atmospheric band that will transport you to outer space and deep into your heart. Fronted by classically trained singer and pianist Molly Hilgenberg, Sister Veery brings together the talents of Shanna Willie on drums, Michael Geraci on bass, Chris Rourke on guitar, and Adeline Wright on vocals. In 2025, Sister Veery released their debut full-length album, Cosmic Relevance, supported by an individual artist grant from the Arrowhead Regional Arts Council. Written over the course of a decade, the album draws inspiration from Hilgenberg’s years living among the redwoods and along the coast of Northern California, pairing expansive soundscapes with reflections on life’s bigger questions. Opening for Sister Veery is beloved Duluth singer-songwriter Eldri Snow. Eldri is a radio host and champion of women in music through her programming on The North 103.3 FM.

events.title: Annual Native American Heritage Day
events.description: The St. Louis County Historical Society, under the guidance of the SLCHS American Indian Advisory Committee, is proud to announce its annual Native American Heritage Day from 11 AM to 3 PM on Saturday, November 14, 2026. The event is free and open to all. Native American Heritage Day gives anyone who is curious the opportunity to see, hear, and taste our regional Ojibwe culture. The theme of this year’s event is Native Creativity. Chat with local Ojibwe artists, view their work, and learn more about how Native identity influences their creativity. There will be opportunities to purchase artwork and make crafts of your own! The Historical Society will also be unveiling the design for our new Lake Superior Ojibwe Gallery, scheduled to open in June 2027. Gary Lundstrom, exhibit designer and fabricator, has constructed a scale model of the new exhibit, which will be on display at the SLCHS table.

events.title: ACLARA Meeting
events.description: Aitkin County Lakes and Rivers Association (aka ACLARA) represents 20 lake associations in Aitkin County. Founded in 2005, ACLARA brings together lake/river associations throughout Aitkin County for the purpose of educating members on keeping its lakes/rivers and shore land healthy for future generations. Meetings are held on the second Saturday, April through October, usually at the Aitkin County Library stating at 9:30 a.m. Members are encouraged to discuss their association’s issues, if any, and share ideas on lake/river management, water quality and conservation matters that impact the waters we all appreciate and enjoy. Communication to the membership is via email. Annual, nonrefundable dues are $25 for one representative and one or two alternates. Dues cover the costs of any pertinent information to keep members informed on important issues, local expert speakers on a variety of topics at the monthly meetings and minimal administrative costs. Individuals who share a common interest in the well-being of our lakes/rivers and are not part of an active lake/river association may also join annually for $25.

events.title: Room for Grief
events.description: A Peer-led gathering on Grief, Gratitude, & Belonging Grief is not a problem to be solved, but an experience to be witnessed. Grief, when shared, becomes a bridge that connects us rather than a burden that isolates us; and offers an opportunity for finding authentic healing. We will speak from personal experience, listen with curiosity, and honor different ways of responding to grief. We will ground ourselves, share what brings us to the space, as well as what we are taking with us as we leave. As our monthly gatherings evolve, participants and community members will be invited to share the particular gifts and skills they have to offer this collective experience of grief. This may include singing, movement, breath work, and other embodied practices. Participants are welcome to bring something to add to the altar that represents their experience of grief. Bio: Paula Williams will hold the space for these peer-led gatherings.

This FREE, family-friendly event is an opportunity to learn together through stories, shared experiences, and cultural traditions while supporting Indigenous artists, educators, and community members. Throughout the day, guests can participate in hands-on printmaking, enjoy an Ojibwe-inspired meal, and experience a vibrant cultural showcase featuring drumming, singing, and dancing. 🥁🎶 Join Fire in the Village, a collective of artists and cultural organizers, for a printmaking pop-up! Participants are invited to make and take a fabric patch featuring images of Aandeg (Crow), the Fire in the Village emblem, and other artwork created by Anishinaabe artist and director Annie Humphrey (Leech Lake Band of Ojibwe).

events.title: Songfield
events.description: Songfield is a gathering space for singing rooted in relational presence. We connect through song, embodiment, and relational mindfulness practices, inviting a more conscious music making experience to deepen our aliveness as we play and create in the group field. We learn simple songs together, including folk, traditional, spiritual, chant, and we allow space for organic musical expression. We explore how becoming more present and attuned to our bodies and with one another can enhance our singing with more truthful expression, love, passion, and a fuller spectrum of our humanness. While we practice together, we also focus on the quality of connection between us, drawing closer to what matters as we cultivate and nourish the ground of relationship from which our singing arises. What a Songfield Gathering Includes · Warming up our voices and bodies. · Learning and singing songs together. · Relational Fielding practices supporting attunement, authenticity, connection, and coherence. · More singing! · Guided healing integration when processes arise organically · Group reflections.

events.description: The opening production for the 2026 – 2027 Theatre North Season is The Dining Room. Synopsis: Set in the dining room of a typical well-to-do household, The Dining Room is a mosaic of interrelated scenes – some funny, some touching, some rueful – which, taken together, create an in-depth portrait of vanishing traditions of the American upper middle class. The actors change roles, as they portray a wide variety of characters, from little boys to stern grandfathers, and from giggling teenage girls to Irish housemaids. Each vignette introduces a new set of people and events (spanning decades): a father lectures his son on grammar and politics; a boy returns from boarding school to discover his mother’s infidelity; a senile grandmother doesn’t recognize her own sons at Christmas dinner; a daughter, her marriage a shambles, pleads futilely to return home. Dovetailing swiftly and smoothly, the varied scenes coalesce, ultimately, into a theatrical experience of exceptional range, compassionate humor and abundant humanity. events.title: Ian Alexy
events.description: Troubadour 21st Century is the new record by singer-songwriter Ian Alexy. Best known for his work with Americana duo Hobo Nephews Of Uncle Frank, Ian expands the possibilities on Troubadour 21st Century with rock grooves and spine-tingling electric guitar flourishes. This is Ian Alexy’s fifth album as a solo artist, in addition to five albums with Hobo Nephews Of Uncle Frank. Hobo Nephews first earned their live reputation by opening a sold-out national tour for Trampled By Turtles before touring all over the United States as a headliner. Their 2015 song Old Number 4 was featured on CBS Sports.com and soon after went viral. Ian has received critical acclaim for his work as a solo artist as well. In addition to performing as a solo artist and with his band Ian Alexy and The Deserters, he is also working on a series of documentaries titled Making It Shine comprised of footage of life on the road and in the studio over the past several years. With the world re opening again the Troubadour 21st Century is ready to return to the music life. “Invokes 80s era Petty and Springsteen.” - Minneapolis Star Tribune “Stomping Blues Rock reminiscent of Dan Auerbach.”

events.title: Urinetown Presented By Zeitgeist Theater Co.
events.description: URINETOWN By Mark Hollmann and Greg Kotis Directed by Robert Lee Musical Direction by Beth Brophy Winner of three Tony Awards, three Outer Critics Circle Awards, two Lucille Lortel Awards and two Obie Awards, Urinetown is a hilarious musical satire of the legal system, capitalism, social irresponsibility, populism, environmental collapse, privatization of natural resources, bureaucracy, municipal politics, and musical theatre itself! Hilariously funny and touchingly honest, Urinetown provides a fresh perspective on one of America’s greatest art forms. In a Gotham-like city, a terrible water shortage, caused by a 20-year drought, has led to a government-enforced ban on private toilets. The citizens must use public amenities, regulated by a single malevolent company that profits by charging admission for one of humanity’s most basic needs. Amid the people, a hero decides that he’s had enough and plans a revolution to lead them all to freedom! Inspired by the works of Bertolt Brecht and Kurt Weill, Urinetown is an irreverently humorous satire in which no one is safe from scrutiny.

events.title: Live Music: Entheos Enclave
events.description: Entheos Enclave is a Duluth based original band fronted by Inga Weis. This Nordic fusion of indie/crossover prog and world music comes from both deep love and deep grief, while moving towards healing. Their lyrics and melodies draw up inspiration from below the surface: emotion, spirituality, and the school of life. Complete with classically-influenced guitar, jazz-influenced piano, bass, drums, backup vox, and Inga’s unique style, a language of its own is created. Their music will have you moving, feeling, and connecting to a meticulous ear and an open heart through complex melodies and cathartic messaging. Following their 2025 debut album "Eschaton", Entheos Enclave has been releasing new music throughout 2026, and they've also produced a band documentary!

events.description: The Leonids meteor shower offers clear-sky meteor rates of about 10 to 15 shooting stars per hour. They are active between Nov. 6 - 30 and will peak on Nov. 17-18. The Leonids are bright meteors and have a high percentage of persistent trains according to AMS. The Leonids' radiant is located in the sickle-shaped head of the constellation Leo, the lion. Leonid meteor hunting can be incredible, or a total bust. It all depends on where its parent body, Comet 55P/Tempel-Tuttle, will be in its orbit and the kind of debris clumps that will be around when our planet passes through this comet's orbit.

events.title: Antique Appraisal
events.description: Bring your antique/collectible item for a free appraisal to the St. Louis County Depot at 506 West Michigan Street, Duluth, Minnesota. The St. Louis County Historical Society has arranged for Denny Mager of Northern Specialty, an expert in antique appraisal, to be at your service beginning at noon in the Union Lounge (outside of the Board Room), which is on street level. Follow event signage. Registration is in person only and cut-off at 2:30PM, so the appraiser can finish appraisals by 3PM. Guests are called up in the order that they are registered. You may bring up to two items per person for an informal oral identification and evaluation of each antique. If the piece is too large or fragile to be hand-carried, clear photographs with a description of any marks and labels will be sufficient. Past participants have thoroughly enjoyed the appraiser’s comments on what is always an interesting assortment of antiques and collectibles. This session is part of an on-going public education program offered by the St. Louis County Historical Society.

events.title: Urinetown Presented By Zeitgeist Theater Co.
events.description: URINETOWN By Mark Hollmann and Greg Kotis Directed by Robert Lee Musical Direction by Beth Brophy Winner of three Tony Awards, three Outer Critics Circle Awards, two Lucille Lortel Awards and two Obie Awards, Urinetown is a hilarious musical satire of the legal system, capitalism, social irresponsibility, populism, environmental collapse, privatization of natural resources, bureaucracy, municipal politics, and musical theatre itself! Hilariously funny and touchingly honest, Urinetown provides a fresh perspective on one of America’s greatest art forms. In a Gotham-like city, a terrible water shortage, caused by a 20-year drought, has led to a government-enforced ban on private toilets. The citizens must use public amenities, regulated by a single malevolent company that profits by charging admission for one of humanity’s most basic needs. Amid the people, a hero decides that he’s had enough and plans a revolution to lead them all to freedom! Inspired by the works of Bertolt Brecht and Kurt Weill, Urinetown is an irreverently humorous satire in which no one is safe from scrutiny.

events.title: DECC 60th Anniversary Gala
events.description: The First-Ever DECC Gala: a Progressive Party through the Decades We’re excited to announce the inaugural DECC Gala, a one-of-a-kind celebration honoring the 60th Anniversary of the DECC. This isn’t your typical gala because the DECC, with 10 community venues, is anything but typical. Guests will embark on a progressive journey through the decades and across the DECC campus, experiencing the history of the organization in a truly immersive way. The evening begins in Symphony Hall, celebrating the 1960s with food, beverages & entertainment inspired by the decade. From there, guests will move throughout the campus, with each venue representing a different era, complete with themed food, drinks, and experiences. The celebration culminates in AMSOIL Arena, where we’ll arrive in the 2020s and toast to the future of the DECC. As this is a progressive party, expect a great deal of walking and the VIP pass will be even more strenuous to access hidden areas. Join us for an unforgettable evening celebrating six decades of memories, milestones, and community impact.

events.title: Urinetown Presented By Zeitgeist Theater Co.
events.description: URINETOWN By Mark Hollmann and Greg Kotis Directed by Robert Lee Musical Direction by Beth Brophy Winner of three Tony Awards, three Outer Critics Circle Awards, two Lucille Lortel Awards and two Obie Awards, Urinetown is a hilarious musical satire of the legal system, capitalism, social irresponsibility, populism, environmental collapse, privatization of natural resources, bureaucracy, municipal politics, and musical theatre itself! Hilariously funny and touchingly honest, Urinetown provides a fresh perspective on one of America’s greatest art forms. In a Gotham-like city, a terrible water shortage, caused by a 20-year drought, has led to a government-enforced ban on private toilets. The citizens must use public amenities, regulated by a single malevolent company that profits by charging admission for one of humanity’s most basic needs. Amid the people, a hero decides that he’s had enough and plans a revolution to lead them all to freedom! Inspired by the works of Bertolt Brecht and Kurt Weill, Urinetown is an irreverently humorous satire in which no one is safe from scrutiny.

events.description: URINETOWN By Mark Hollmann and Greg Kotis Directed by Robert Lee Musical Direction by Beth Brophy Winner of three Tony Awards, three Outer Critics Circle Awards, two Lucille Lortel Awards and two Obie Awards, Urinetown is a hilarious musical satire of the legal system, capitalism, social irresponsibility, populism, environmental collapse, privatization of natural resources, bureaucracy, municipal politics, and musical theatre itself! Hilariously funny and touchingly honest, Urinetown provides a fresh perspective on one of America’s greatest art forms. In a Gotham-like city, a terrible water shortage, caused by a 20-year drought, has led to a government-enforced ban on private toilets. The citizens must use public amenities, regulated by a single malevolent company that profits by charging admission for one of humanity’s most basic needs. Amid the people, a hero decides that he’s had enough and plans a revolution to lead them all to freedom! Inspired by the works of Bertolt Brecht and Kurt Weill, Urinetown is an irreverently humorous satire in which no one is safe from scrutiny.

events.title: Music Then and Now Concert: Eveleth Public Library
events.description: Free Solo String Concerts to tour local ALS libraries this November and December The Arrowhead Library System is pleased to present free concerts at participating ALS libraries November 17 - December 18, 2026. This music event, presented by musician Sara Pajunen, is titled: Music Then and Now: a Solo String Concert . Join Sara Pajunen on a tour of classical, folk, and original music on violin and hardanger d'amore, a ten-string bow instrument. This concert showcases Sara's musical repertoire and original compositions, inspired by travels abroad and grounded in her childhood on the Iron Range. This program is 50 minutes long and suited for adults and children of all ages. These free programs are being offered at the following locations: Tuesday, November 17, 1:00 p.m. - Ely Public Library Wednesday, November 18, 6:30 p.m. - International Falls Public Library Thursday, November 19, 10:00 a.m. - CHI Lakewood Care Center, hosted by Baudette Public Library Friday, November 20, 10:00 a.m. - Mountain Iron Public Library Friday, November 20, 3:30 p.m. - Buhl Public Library Saturday, November 21, 10:00 a.m. - Eveleth Public Library Wednesday, December 2, 10:00 a.m.

events.title: Ian Alexy: Every Third Saturday at Sir Ben's
events.venue: Sir Benedicts Tavern on the Lake
events.description: Ian Alexy plays solo acoustic (with looping and effects, of course) on the third Saturday of every month at Sir Benedict's in Duluth. Troubadour 21st Century is the new record by singer-songwriter Ian Alexy. Best known for his work with Americana duo Hobo Nephews Of Uncle Frank, Ian expands the possibilities on Troubadour 21st Century with rock grooves and spine-tingling electric guitar flourishes. This is Ian Alexy’s fifth album as a solo artist, in addition to five albums with Hobo Nephews Of Uncle Frank. Hobo Nephews first earned their live reputation by opening a sold-out national tour for Trampled By Turtles before touring all over the United States as a headliner. Their 2015 song Old Number 4 was featured on CBS Sports.com and soon after went viral. Ian has received critical acclaim for his work as a solo artist as well. In addition to performing as a solo artist and with his band Ian Alexy and The Deserters, he is also working on a series of documentaries titled Making It Shine comprised of footage of life on the road and in the studio over the past several years. With the world re opening again the Troubadour 21st Century is ready to return to the music life.

events.title: Urinetown Presented By Zeitgeist Theater Co.
events.description: URINETOWN By Mark Hollmann and Greg Kotis Directed by Robert Lee Musical Direction by Beth Brophy Winner of three Tony Awards, three Outer Critics Circle Awards, two Lucille Lortel Awards and two Obie Awards, Urinetown is a hilarious musical satire of the legal system, capitalism, social irresponsibility, populism, environmental collapse, privatization of natural resources, bureaucracy, municipal politics, and musical theatre itself! Hilariously funny and touchingly honest, Urinetown provides a fresh perspective on one of America’s greatest art forms. In a Gotham-like city, a terrible water shortage, caused by a 20-year drought, has led to a government-enforced ban on private toilets. The citizens must use public amenities, regulated by a single malevolent company that profits by charging admission for one of humanity’s most basic needs. Amid the people, a hero decides that he’s had enough and plans a revolution to lead them all to freedom! Inspired by the works of Bertolt Brecht and Kurt Weill, Urinetown is an irreverently humorous satire in which no one is safe from scrutiny.

events.title: Sunhee's Little Table - Authentic Korean Food Truck
events.description: Sunhee’s Little Table at Bent Paddle 🍜 Sunhee’s Little Table is bringing authentic Korean flavors to Bent Paddle for a pop-up you won’t want to miss. Come grab a pint (or THC bev) and dig into some seriously good, made-from-scratch Korean comfort food. Here’s a taste of what they’ll be serving up: Bulgogi (불고기) Thinly sliced beef marinated in a savory mix of soy sauce, garlic, sesame oil, and a touch of sweetness—then grilled to perfection. Rich, flavorful, and made for pairing with a cold beer. Tteokbokki (떡볶이) A Korean street food favorite featuring chewy rice cakes in a spicy-sweet chili sauce. Bold, comforting, and just the right amount of heat. Bulgogi Kimbap (불고기 김밥) Korean-style rolls packed with marinated bulgogi, fresh veggies, and rice, all wrapped in seaweed. Easy to snack on and perfect alongside your favorite Bent Paddle pour. Come hungry, grab a drink, and enjoy something a little different in the Taproom.

events.description: 1st of 3 supermoons in a row A perigee is when the moon 's orbit is closest to the earth and a supermoon is when the full or new moon coincide (or almost coincide) with the perigee. What does that mean? The moon looks exceptionally big because it is close! Full moons have many names derived from various cultures reflecting what was happening in the natural world. While the Frost Moon and Freezing Moon are self-explanatory, November's full moon is most known as the Beaver Moon. Beavers are quite active preparing for winter. Also known as the Mourning Moon, due to the increase in darkness.

Gather your friends and test your wits as you try to guess the initials of famous people, places, and things. It's FREE! There’s no cost to play, and tons of great prizes for the winners (we even have prizes for non-winners!) HOW TO PLAY: 1. Gather your friends - Bring a crew of your favorite companions to the nearest Initials Game Live location. 2. Listen to the clues - You’ll hear six clues per item. They start out tricky, but don’t worry! They get progressively easier. 3. Submit your guess - The sooner you submit the correct answer, the more points you get. If you guess wrong, you’re out until the next item. 4. Tally them up! - Each round contains five items. A full game consists of three rounds. Prizes awarded at the end of each round!

events.title: Mason Jennings
events.description: Mason Jennings is a Minnesota-based pop-folk singer-songwriter. Jennings is originally from Honolulu, Hawaii. He is well known for his simple yet catchy melodies, intimate lyrics, intensely literary and historical themes, and deep tenor's voice. His music has appeared in the surf film Shelter and he has toured extensively. Jennings is married to Amy Jennings (nee Turany) and has a son, August, born in January 2003. Jennings produced his self-titled debut album in 1997 on an analog four-track in the basement of a rented home, manning all instruments himself. In October 1998, after bringing drummer Chris Stock and bassist Robert Skoro on board, he began a weekly gig at Minneapolis' 400 Bar as the Mason Jennings Band. Garnering local praise and a wide fan base, Mason began touring nationally. His 2000 album Birds Flying Away revealed Jennings' political activism and penchant for singing first-person narratives of imaginary rustic characters. Following the release of this album, Noah Levy took over drumming duties from Stock. 2002 saw the release of two albums: the studio piece Century Spring and a "fans only" collection of acoustic rarities, Simple Life.

events.title: Shane Nelson - Havannas (Superior WI)
events.description: Live music with songwriter Shane Nelson -grab some authentic Cubin food, a drink and a seat, and enjoy an evening of listening. Shane Nelson is a singer, songwriter, musician, and producer who has been following his artistic instincts to create since he was a child. Nelson started performing at school and community events when he was 8 years old. In his teens, Nelson built the band, “Crescent Moon”. Along with his band, Shane has earned recognition as one of the Northland’s top local musical acts by winning several battle of the bands competitions, being voted the Northland’s best live musical act by local radio stations, and through live performances throughout the Midwest. Nelson’s band has performed alongside nationally recognized acts such as Survivor, Toad the Wet Sprocket, and Confederate Railroad. As a solo artist, Shane has been featured on PBS television, has won several singer/songwriter contests, and earned the title of Northland Idol through a local ABC Television affiliate which landed him in Nashville, TN. Although Nelson has won several awards and has received recognition for his musical abilities, he is not in it for the eminence.

events.title: Iron Range Night
events.description: The Iron Range Rocks! Celebrate the music from Minnesota’s Iron Range with performances from The Brothers Burn Mountain, Hobo Revival and The Sectionals beginning at 7 p.m. Saturday, Nov. 28. Guitar and drum duo Ryan and Jesse Dermody have been performing as The Brothers Burn Mountain for 25 years. Based out of their off-the-grid, self-constructed studio near Cotton, the duo has toured relentlessly around the midwest for more than two decades. The Brothers Burn Mountain have released 11 full-length albums of original music and released a “best of” collection in 2025. Hobo Revival, based out of Nashauk, has been performing their straight-ahead brand of rock and roll across northern Minnesota for 15 years. Led by singer-songwriter Kim Nagler, the group released its latest album “The Pulled Pork Sessions” in 2024. The Sectionals are a vocal octet performing classic jazz and modern acapella favorites. The ensemble features members from throughout the Iron Range. This event is made possible in part by a grant from the Arrowhead Regional Arts Council with funds appropriated from the Minnesota Legislature from its General Fund.

events.description: Sunhee’s Little Table at Bent Paddle 🍜 Sunhee’s Little Table is bringing authentic Korean flavors to Bent Paddle for a pop-up you won’t want to miss. Come grab a pint (or THC bev) and dig into some seriously good, made-from-scratch Korean comfort food. Here’s a taste of what they’ll be serving up: Bulgogi (불고기) Thinly sliced beef marinated in a savory mix of soy sauce, garlic, sesame oil, and a touch of sweetness—then grilled to perfection. Rich, flavorful, and made for pairing with a cold beer. Tteokbokki (떡볶이) A Korean street food favorite featuring chewy rice cakes in a spicy-sweet chili sauce. Bold, comforting, and just the right amount of heat. Bulgogi Kimbap (불고기 김밥) Korean-style rolls packed with marinated bulgogi, fresh veggies, and rice, all wrapped in seaweed. Easy to snack on and perfect alongside your favorite Bent Paddle pour. Come hungry, grab a drink, and enjoy something a little different in the Taproom.

From "Haven't Met You Yet" to "Home" and "Sway" to "Feeling Good," every song is delivered with bold new arrangements, boundless energy and Shaun's Entertainer of the Year stylings. Billboard Top 5 artist and Emmy Award winner. "Shaun Johnson splits the difference between the dulcet urbanity of Michael Bublé and the campy yowl of the Stray Cats’ Brian Setzer. He fronts a brassy octet he dubs Shaun Johnson’s Big Band Experience (he’s also the lead singer of Tonic Sol-fa and Shaun Sings Country). A retro nerd of Rat Pack vintage, his performances go for the gut in rousing fashion.” ~ Minneapolis Star Tribune The Shaun Johnson Big Band Experience is a rare newcomer to traditional pop...fusing a big band spirit with an inventive edge...at once more risky than Buble, more modern than Sinatra.

events.title: Sunhee's Little Table - Authentic Korean Food Truck
events.description: Sunhee’s Little Table at Bent Paddle 🍜 Sunhee’s Little Table is bringing authentic Korean flavors to Bent Paddle for a pop-up you won’t want to miss. Come grab a pint (or THC bev) and dig into some seriously good, made-from-scratch Korean comfort food. Here’s a taste of what they’ll be serving up: Bulgogi (불고기) Thinly sliced beef marinated in a savory mix of soy sauce, garlic, sesame oil, and a touch of sweetness—then grilled to perfection. Rich, flavorful, and made for pairing with a cold beer. Tteokbokki (떡볶이) A Korean street food favorite featuring chewy rice cakes in a spicy-sweet chili sauce. Bold, comforting, and just the right amount of heat. Bulgogi Kimbap (불고기 김밥) Korean-style rolls packed with marinated bulgogi, fresh veggies, and rice, all wrapped in seaweed. Easy to snack on and perfect alongside your favorite Bent Paddle pour. Come hungry, grab a drink, and enjoy something a little different in the Taproom.

events.title: Community Sing
events.description: Join us on the first Tuesday of every month for community singing. Simply show up (registration is not required) and join the circle of voices. Music will be taught the night of; all voices are welcome to gather and be led in song. There are no auditions or music to read, no performances, and little to no accompanying instrumentation. Community Sing is an entirely oral tradition for people of all ages! Unlike a choir, Community Sing is not divided by traditional voice parts or vocal range. Some songs are sung all together, as call-and-response, in a round, or in taught parts. Community Sing is also non-denominational. This recurring monthly event has no cover charge, though donations are always appreciated. Thank you Chickadee-Dee-Dee for leading us in song!

events.title: The Initials Game Live
events.description: Wednesdays at Duluth Cider come try the new hit bar trivia game, The Initials Game Live, made famous on KFAN radio! The Initials Game Live is a fun and competitive general knowledge and pop culture party game for players of all skill levels. Gather your friends and test your wits as you try to guess the initials of famous people, places, and things. It's FREE! There’s no cost to play, and tons of great prizes for the winners (we even have prizes for non-winners!) HOW TO PLAY: 1. Gather your friends - Bring a crew of your favorite companions to the nearest Initials Game Live location. 2. Listen to the clues - You’ll hear six clues per item. They start out tricky, but don’t worry! They get progressively easier. 3. Submit your guess - The sooner you submit the correct answer, the more points you get. If you guess wrong, you’re out until the next item. 4. Tally them up! - Each round contains five items. A full game consists of three rounds. Prizes awarded at the end of each round!

events.title: Veterans Memorial Hall Annual Remembrance Dinner on 12/03/2026
events.description: Purchase Tickets Online Join us for the 21st annual Veterans Memorial Hall Remembrance Dinner on Thursday, December 3, 2026, in the Great Hall at the St. Louis County Depot. This year’s keynote presentation, “Shipbuilding in the Twin Ports During World War II,” will be presented by Stephen B. Daniel. During World War II, shipyards throughout Duluth and Superior built military and support vessels for the war effort. Stephen Daniel will explore where these ships were built, the types of vessels produced, and the people who worked in the local shipyards, including the important role women played as many men left the region for military service. The evening begins with a social hour at 5:00 p.m., followed by dinner at 6:00 p.m. and the keynote presentation at 7:00 p.m. Dinner will be catered by Valentini’s, and guests may also participate in a silent auction. Tickets are $65 per person. Join us for an evening of remembrance and local history, highlighting the remarkable contribution the Twin Ports made to America’s World War II effort.

Tickets are $8 for adults and $5 for students. Thank you to our movie sponsor: Wakefield Winter Wonderlights! Synopsis: On Christmas Eve, a skeptical young boy begins to doubt the existence of Santa Claus. Just before midnight, a mysterious steam train known as the Polar Express abruptly pulls up outside his home. Invited aboard by the enigmatic Conductor, he joins a group of other children on an extraordinary journey to the North Pole. Along the track, the children encounter daunting obstacles, strange wilderness figures, and moments that test their courage and friendship. Upon reaching the heart of Santa’s sprawling city, the young protagonist learns that the true magic of Christmas lies not in what you see, but in what you choose to believe—symbolized by a silver sleigh bell whose ring can only be heard by those who truly believe.

events.title: Shane Nelson - Havanas
events.description: Cuban food and songwriting, From Shane Nelson Shane Nelson is a singer, songwriter, musician, and producer who has been following his artistic instincts to create since he was a child. Nelson started performing at school and community events when he was 8 years old. In his teens, Nelson built the band, “Crescent Moon”. Along with his band, Shane has earned recognition as one of the Northland’s top local musical acts by winning several battle of the bands competitions, being voted the Northland’s best live musical act by local radio stations, and through live performances throughout the Midwest. Nelson’s band has performed alongside nationally recognized acts such as Survivor, Toad the Wet Sprocket, and Confederate Railroad. As a solo artist, Shane has been featured on PBS television, has won several singer/songwriter contests, and earned the title of Northland Idol through a local ABC Television affiliate which landed him in Nashville, TN. Although Nelson has won several awards and has received recognition for his musical abilities, he is not in it for the eminence.

events.title: Iron County Historical Museum
events.description: Plan an adventure at the Iron County Historical Society Museum. Built in 1893 as the town hall for the now-vanished Town of Vaughn, the museum building was sold the following April to serve as the courthouse of Iron County. The Museum offers you three full floors of display from history of iron mining to railroads, timber to veterans, home life to faith based articles. The museum is filled with many old photos showing life in the past. May thru October MON/WED/FRI/SAT 1OAM-2PM, NOVEMBER - APRIL WED/FRI/SAT.

events.title: Ely Area Writer’s Group
events.description: The mission of the Ely Area Writers Group (formerly Writers Read) is to encourage writers to write. Writers tend to hide their work. For most, the only thing worse than rejection is having something printed that isn’t perfect, so we give gentle suggestions for edits and cheer all the good bits. When someone joins our group, we add their email to our list. Before our monthly meetings, anyone can submit something they’ve written to the group via email. Any genre is welcome. The author may be specific about what response they want (does this essay flow, or is this character believable, or which images stick with you?) or they can let the others respond on any aspect that strikes them. Some members submit work every month, others may share something only a few times a year. Registration is not required; simply show up!

events.title: Gag Me With A Spoon
events.description: A celebration of stories, voices, and gestures. Offering a fun and safe space to hear stories and confessions, musings and triumphs of the human experience ranging from thrift store shopping to grand awakenings. You can expect an evening of tears and laughter, song and connection. Since our start 13 years ago, this show has evolved into a staple for our community. It’s a unique space where local and regional folks share their most vulnerable, hilarious and triumphant moments. We focus on authentic, unscripted human connection—the kind of intimacy that knits community in real time. Looking forward to it!

events.title: John Louis
events.venue: Sir Benedicts Tavern on the Lake
events.description: Country troubadour John Louis wanders around this world of music, writing and singing heartworn country folk songs. John’s that guy on the bus who sits quietly, looking tired like the rest of us. The difference is he is sitting there composing a song about your life and those painful poignant moments you dust off on the way home between life’s chores. His songs show us our lives and the subtle but important things that become universally important hallmarks of our Midwestern journey. Like church basement rolls at the funeral. Like the small moments on road trips filled with meaning, loss and memory. The tragedies and triumphs that break us and keep us going one more day. John glimpses it all through a poet’s heart. When he stands bravely on a stage with a guitar and begins singing, we get to see it too. And it makes sense for a moment. The songs John writes keep winning awards from prestigious songwriting showcases. Including the Kerrville Folk Festival New Folk competition, Rocky Mountain Folks Festival Songwriter Showcase, and the Great River Folk Fest songwriter contest. (That’s some hot sh-t folks!)

Nov 11 Yesteryear, Caro Claire Burke Dec 9 Mrs. Caliban, Rachel Ingalls Jan 13 The Tiger’s Wife, Tea Obreht Feb 10 Small things Like These, Claire Keegan March 10 Life After Life, Kate Atkinson April 14 Sea of Tranquility, Emily St. John Mandel Everyone Welcome. You do not need to “join.” Come whenever it works or the book strikes your fancy. The Book Bar will be open serving wine, cider, beer & NA drinks + sandwiches and pizzas. Claire Duquette is the former editor of the Ashland Daily Press and continues to write about books and the arts. She is the assistant manager at Honest Dog Books where you’ll find her behind the counter Saturdays selecting books for the store’s SurpriseMe! Subscription. Ellen Akins is the author of the novels Home Movie (1988), Little Woman (1990), Public Life (1993), and Hometown Brew (1998), and the short story collection World Like a Knife (1991). She writes book reviews for national publications like the Washington Post and Star Tribune and loves talking books. Recurring monthly on the 2nd Wednesday.

events.description: Wild Roots Learning Community 📅 Dates: Sep. 10, Sep. 24, Oct. 8, Oct. 22, Nov. 12, Dec. 10 (all Thursdays) ⏰ Time: 10:00am-12:00pm (each time) 👧 Age Range: 3-12 y/o (younger/older siblings welcome!) 💵 Cost: $5/kid 3-and-older ⭐ FREE for MDC Members, kids 2-and-under, and accompanying grown-ups Wild Roots is a play-based learning group where kids discover the world around them through child-led exploration. This year, we’re exploring forces—wind, gravity, water, weight, and balance. A little wild. A little wobbly. events.title: Community Sing
events.description: Join us on the first Tuesday of every month for community singing. Simply show up (registration is not required) and join the circle of voices. Music will be taught the night of; all voices are welcome to gather and be led in song. There are no auditions or music to read, no performances, and little to no accompanying instrumentation. Community Sing is an entirely oral tradition for people of all ages! Unlike a choir, Community Sing is not divided by traditional voice parts or vocal range. Some songs are sung all together, as call-and-response, in a round, or in taught parts. Community Sing is also non-denominational.

events.title: J Streitz and the Long Odds: J Streitz | The Ore House
events.description: J Streitz plays original folk/Americana songs along with a few covers by great songwriters including John Prine, Todd Snider, and Bob Dylan. While playing bass in several Minneapolis bands spanning over two decades, Jason Streitz quietly wrote country, bluegrass and folk songs in his spare time. These songs, along with a handful of new tunes would become the foundation for The Long Odds. In October of 2016 the band recorded their first full length record with engineer Nick Tveitbakk at the renowned Pachyderm Studios in Cannon Falls, MN. Level Ground was released in the winter of 2018 with special guests Jimmy Rogers and fiddle player Allie Kral (Yonder Mountain String Band) contributing their talents. In August of 2019 Jason moved with his family from Minneapolis to the north woods of Wisconsin where they now own and operate a small pottery business out of an old 1921 schoolhouse, Brickyard Pottery and Gallery. Operating now as Jason Streitz and the Long Odds the band is eager to complete their 2nd full length album. The bones of album #2 were recorded in June of 2019 at The Hideaway Studios in NE Minneapolis and is set to be released in the Winter of 2021.

events.title: J Streitz and the Long Odds: J Streitz & Jimmy Rogers | Sir Bens Tavern

events.description: J Streitz and Jimmy Rogers play original Midwest folk/Americana music. Expect grounded, rootsy tunes, a few familiar covers, and a night that feels relaxed and genuine. While playing bass in several Minneapolis bands spanning over two decades, Jason Streitz quietly wrote country, bluegrass and folk songs in his spare time. These songs, along with a handful of new tunes would become the foundation for The Long Odds. In October of 2016 the band recorded their first full length record with engineer Nick Tveitbakk at the renowned Pachyderm Studios in Cannon Falls, MN. Level Ground was released in the winter of 2018 with special guests Jimmy Rogers and fiddle player Allie Kral (Yonder Mountain String Band) contributing their talents. In August of 2019 Jason moved with his family from Minneapolis to the north woods of Wisconsin where they now own and operate a small pottery business out of an old 1921 schoolhouse, Brickyard Pottery and Gallery. Operating now as Jason Streitz and the Long Odds the band is eager to complete their 2nd full length album.

events.title: ACLARA Meeting
events.description: Aitkin County Lakes and Rivers Association (aka ACLARA) represents 20 lake associations in Aitkin County. Founded in 2005, ACLARA brings together lake/river associations throughout Aitkin County for the purpose of educating members on keeping its lakes/rivers and shore land healthy for future generations. Meetings are held on the second Saturday, April through October, usually at the Aitkin County Library stating at 9:30 a.m. Members are encouraged to discuss their association’s issues, if any, and share ideas on lake/river management, water quality and conservation matters that impact the waters we all appreciate and enjoy. Communication to the membership is via email. Annual, nonrefundable dues are $25 for one representative and one or two alternates. Dues cover the costs of any pertinent information to keep members informed on important issues, local expert speakers on a variety of topics at the monthly meetings and minimal administrative costs. Individuals who share a common interest in the well-being of our lakes/rivers and are not part of an active lake/river association may also join annually for $25.

events.title: GB Leighton
events.description: The Event Center, Floodwood GB Leighton acoustic show The Event Center, Floodwood 201 West 7th Avenue Floodwood, MN 55736 More than 200 shows a year. Jubilant fans who follow him from Minnesota to Mexico. More than 100,000 albums sold. A new release “Get Up” and a state-of-the-art nightclub named after one of his songs -- all without the support of a major record label... Meet GB Leighton, a band named after one of the regions’ most incendiary live performers and consistently solid songwriters, Brian Leighton. Through more than a decade and eleven studio albums, Leighton and his five piece band have been tearing up rock clubs, festivals and even a few fan’s living rooms with a slew of songs that connect with the heart and couples singing along out on the dance floor. “A man of the people” is a phrase usually reserved for statesmen and politicians, but for Leighton, it’s a fitting description when you see him in action working a crowd. Leighton delivers that same inescapable rock ‘n’ roll spirit night after night. “If I hadn’t heard a bunch of Bruce’s bootlegs or seen the videos I’d be a much different musician,” he says today.

Join an all-star cast of musicians as they rock their way through timeless holiday classics and bring new takes on hit songs you didn’t even know were holiday classics. The line-up of musicians is truly legendary as Paul “Stretch” Diethelm and Ted Manderfeld are joined on stage by vocalists Pamela McNeill, Stacy Bauer, and Tim Haussner, and backed by bassist Mike Zeleny, saxophonist and flutist Mike Kreitzer and drummer Billy Thommes. events.title: The Initials Game Live
events.description: Wednesdays at Duluth Cider come try the new hit bar trivia game, The Initials Game Live, made famous on KFAN radio! The Initials Game Live is a fun and competitive general knowledge and pop culture party game for players of all skill levels. Gather your friends and test your wits as you try to guess the initials of famous people, places, and things. It's FREE! There’s no cost to play, and tons of great prizes for the winners (we even have prizes for non-winners!) HOW TO PLAY: 1. Gather your friends - Bring a crew of your favorite companions to the nearest Initials Game Live location. 2. Listen to the clues - You’ll hear six clues per item. They start out tricky, but don’t worry! They get progressively easier. 3. Submit your guess - The sooner you submit the correct answer, the more points you get. If you guess wrong, you’re out until the next item. 4. Tally them up! - Each round contains five items. A full game consists of three rounds. Prizes awarded at the end of each round!

events.title: J Streitz and the Long Odds: J Streitz | Ursa Minor Brewing
events.description: J Streitz plays original Midwest Americana music along with a few covers. Expect grounded, rootsy tunes, a few familiar covers, and a night that feels relaxed and genuine. While playing bass in several Minneapolis bands spanning over two decades, Jason Streitz quietly wrote country, bluegrass and folk songs in his spare time. These songs, along with a handful of new tunes would become the foundation for The Long Odds. In October of 2016 the band recorded their first full length record with engineer Nick Tveitbakk at the renowned Pachyderm Studios in Cannon Falls, MN. Level Ground was released in the winter of 2018 with special guests Jimmy Rogers and fiddle player Allie Kral (Yonder Mountain String Band) contributing their talents. In August of 2019 Jason moved with his family from Minneapolis to the north woods of Wisconsin where they now own and operate a small pottery business out of an old 1921 schoolhouse, Brickyard Pottery and Gallery. Operating now as Jason Streitz and the Long Odds the band is eager to complete their 2nd full length album.

events.title: Drooling Pianos
events.description: Thursday, December 17 | DECC Symphony Hall | 7:00pm ON SALE NOW Superior native and professional pianist Russ King and stand-up comedian Chris Covert are bringing Drooling Pianos, their adults-only comedy and music show, to DECC Symphony Hall for a special holiday performance Thursday, December 17 at 7 p.m. Drooling Pianos combines live music, stand-up comedy, original and parody songs, improvisation and audience interaction into an unpredictable show built around the very different backgrounds of its two performers. King is an accomplished pianist, songwriter and producer with a career spanning live performance, recording and touring. Covert comes from the world of stand-up comedy and has performed alongside nationally known comedians including Jeff Ross. Put the two together, and things got hilariously inappropriate pretty quickly. King and Covert only met in February 2026, but what began as an experiment combining live music and stand-up comedy quickly gained an audience. Drooling Pianos has already sold out multiple performances, including its debut, and received an enthusiastic response during its Twin Ports appearance at Clyde Iron Works this summer.

events.description: Ian Alexy plays solo acoustic (with looping and effects, of course) on the third Saturday of every month at Sir Benedict's in Duluth. Troubadour 21st Century is the new record by singer-songwriter Ian Alexy. Best known for his work with Americana duo Hobo Nephews Of Uncle Frank, Ian expands the possibilities on Troubadour 21st Century with rock grooves and spine-tingling electric guitar flourishes. This is Ian Alexy’s fifth album as a solo artist, in addition to five albums with Hobo Nephews Of Uncle Frank. Hobo Nephews first earned their live reputation by opening a sold-out national tour for Trampled By Turtles before touring all over the United States as a headliner. Their 2015 song Old Number 4 was featured on CBS Sports.com and soon after went viral. Ian has received critical acclaim for his work as a solo artist as well. In addition to performing as a solo artist and with his band Ian Alexy and The Deserters, he is also working on a series of documentaries titled Making It Shine comprised of footage of life on the road and in the studio over the past several years. With the world re opening again the Troubadour 21st Century is ready to return to the music life.

events.description: 2nd of 3 supermoons in a row A perigee is when the moon 's orbit is closest to the earth and a supermoon is when the full or new moon coincide (or almost coincide) with the perigee. What does that mean? The moon looks exceptionally big because it is close! Full moons have many names derived from various cultures reflecting what was happening in the natural world. December's full moon is known as the Cold Moon or Long Nights Moon. In addition to the shortest daylight day of the year, the Long Nights Moon pertains to the amount of time the moon is above the horizon. It takes a high trajectory across the sky because it is opposite to the low sun.
